title: Supreme Court Hands Trump Even More Power

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在早上4点30分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中走过七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都使用不同的首字母单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一个平底锅的菜谱，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅即可享受特别优惠，网址为 nytimes.com 加上 subscribe。

sentences.en: Well, this was a big one, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一件大事，不是吗？

sentences.en: This was a big decision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重大的决定。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的蕾切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: This morning the Supreme Court has delivered a monumental victory for the Constitution, the separation of powers, and the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 今天上午，最高法院为宪法、三权分立和法治做出了意义重大的裁决。

sentences.en: In a major ruling on Friday, the Supreme Court limited the ability of judges to block President Trump's policies nationwide, including his order to end birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 在周五的一项重大裁决中，最高法院限制了法官在全国范围内阻止特朗普总统政策的能力，包括他关于结束出生公民权的行政命令。

sentences.en: I'm grateful to the Supreme Court for stepping in and solving this very, very big and complex problem, and they've made it very simple.
sentences.zh: 我感谢最高法院介入并解决这个非常、非常重大且复杂的问题，他们让事情变得非常简单。

sentences.en: The ruling was immediately cheered by the president.
sentences.zh: 该裁决立即受到了总统的欢呼。

sentences.en: It is a big blow to our ability to enforce our rights.
sentences.zh: 这对我们执行权利的能力是一个沉重打击。

sentences.en: While critics have decried it as a fundamental threat to the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 而批评者则谴责这是对法治的根本威胁。

sentences.en: But this is just chaos that they've unleashed in the judicial system for no reason at all.
sentences.zh: 但这只是他们在司法系统中无缘无故引发的混乱。

sentences.en: That kind of ruling establishes not just an imperial executive, but an imperial Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这种裁决不仅确立了一个帝王般的行政权，还确立了一个帝王般的最高法院。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Adam Liptak explains how the ruling redefines the role of the courts at a moment when the White House is aggressively testing the limits of its power.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事亚当·利普塔克将解释在白宫正大举试探其权力极限的时刻，这项裁决如何重新定义了法院的角色。

sentences.en: It's Monday, June 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月30日，星期一。

sentences.en: Adam, we're talking to you just a couple days after the ruling by the Supreme Court in this birthright citizenship case.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我们是在最高法院就这起出生公民权案做出裁决几天后来采访你的。

sentences.en: And the ruling has pretty big implications, not just for the case, but really for the role of the courts and also for a presidency
sentences.zh: 这项裁决具有相当深远的影响，不仅对这个案件本身，而且对法院的角色以及一个总统任期而言

sentences.en: that has been testing the limits of its power and of the law since President Trump took office back in January.
sentences.zh: 自从特朗普总统在一月份上任以来，这个总统任期一直在试探其权力和法律的极限。

sentences.en: Yeah, the decision has a lot of moving pieces, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 是的，这个决定有很多变数，蕾切尔。

sentences.en: And as you say, it's nominally about birthright citizenship, but really it's about the power of the courts to check the president.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它名义上是关于出生公民权的，但实际上关乎法院制衡总统的权力。

sentences.en: And the court gave President Trump a big victory.
sentences.zh: 法院给了特朗普总统一次重大胜利。

sentences.en: It severely limited the ability of lower court judges to stop him from pursuing his ambitious agenda.
sentences.zh: 它极大地限制了下级法院法官阻止他推进雄心勃勃的议程的能力。

sentences.en: Can you just remind us, what are the basics of the case and how did the court arrive at the decision that it did?
sentences.zh: 你能提醒我们一下，这个案件的基本情况是什么，法院是如何做出这一决定的吗？

sentences.en: So on assuming office, President Trump issued an executive order purporting to put an end to birthright citizenship, a fundamental constitutional value in the 14th Amendment
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普总统在上任时发布了一项行政命令，旨在终结出生公民权，这是第十四修正案中一个基本的宪法价值

sentences.en: that says if you're born in the United States, you're a United States citizen.
sentences.zh: 它规定如果你在美国出生，你就是美国公民。

sentences.en: And that's a very bold thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大胆的举动。

sentences.en: It was promptly challenged.
sentences.zh: 它很快受到了挑战。

sentences.en: And three different federal judges in Maryland, in Massachusetts, in Washington state, issued preliminary injunctions blocking the executive order.
sentences.zh: 马里兰州、马萨诸塞州和华盛顿州的三个不同联邦法官发布了初步禁令，阻止了该行政命令。

sentences.en: And the case makes its way to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 随后该案一路诉至最高法院。

sentences.en: The lawyer for the Trump administration does something odd.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府的律师做了一件奇怪的事。

sentences.en: He says, I'm not challenging in the Supreme Court the constitutionality or not of birthright citizenship, but I think these lower court judges did something wrong.
sentences.zh: 他说，我在最高法院不挑战出生公民权是否合宪，但我认为这些下级法院法官做错了事。

sentences.en: They issued what people called nationwide injunctions, sometimes called universal injunctions.
sentences.zh: 他们发布了人们所谓的全国性禁令，有时被称为普遍禁令。

sentences.en: And just remind people what that means exactly.
sentences.zh: 请提醒大家这到底是什么意思。

sentences.en: A universal injunction goes beyond the parties to the case.
sentences.zh: 普遍禁令超出了案件当事人的范围。

sentences.en: It says, I'm a judge.
sentences.zh: 它是说，我是一名法官。

sentences.en: I rule in your favor.
sentences.zh: 我裁决对你有利。

sentences.en: And because you're right that this government policy is unconstitutional,
sentences.zh: 并且因为你认为这项政府政策违宪是正确的，

sentences.en: I'm going to give relief not only to you, but to everybody else affected by the policy.
sentences.zh: 我不仅要向你提供救济，还要向受该政策影响的所有其他人提供救济。

sentences.en: And that is a fairly recent development that there should be such broad injunctions.
sentences.zh: 这种如此广泛的禁令是一个相当近期的发展。

sentences.en: Let's remember, Rachel, this is not the only executive order that courts have found unlawful.
sentences.zh: 蕾切尔，我们要记住，这并不是法院裁定违法的唯一行政命令。

sentences.en: There have been more than 25 universal injunctions on the president's efforts to shut down agencies, to cut funding, to fire federal workers, to bar transgender service members,
sentences.zh: 在总统关闭机构、削减资金、解雇联邦员工、禁止跨性别军人服役等方面的努力上，

sentences.en: to deport hundreds of thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 以及驱逐数十万人的行动中，已经有超过25项普遍禁令。

sentences.en: This is a major, major clash between this administration and lots and lots of federal trial court judges.
sentences.zh: 这是现政府与众多联邦初审法院法官之间的一场重大、重大的冲突。

sentences.en: And as you said, the White House came to the Supreme Court not asking them to rule on whether the executive order on birthright citizenship was constitutional,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，白宫来到最高法院并不是要求他们裁决关于出生公民权的行政命令是否合宪，

sentences.en: which I suspect they think they don't really have a good shot of prevailing at anyway.
sentences.zh: 我猜他们认为自己在该问题上赢面不大。

sentences.en: Instead, the government is coming to the Supreme Court with the intent of going after these nationwide injunctions.
sentences.zh: 相反，政府来到最高法院的意图是针对这些全国性禁令。

sentences.en: Yeah, the consensus view of legal experts is that the administration's arguments on birthright citizenship as such are quite weak.
sentences.zh: 是的，法律专家的共识是，政府在出生公民权本身的论点上相当薄弱。

sentences.en: So they thought, what the hell?
sentences.zh: 所以他们想，管他呢？

sentences.en: We will do what many other cases have done, ask the court to decide whether nationwide injunctions are proper.
sentences.zh: 我们将像许多其他案件所做的那样，要求法院裁定全国性禁令是否恰当。

sentences.en: No presidents like nationwide injunctions.
sentences.zh: 没有哪个总统喜欢全国性禁令。

sentences.en: The Biden administration didn't like them.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府不喜欢它们。

sentences.en: The Trump administration didn't like them.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府不喜欢它们。

sentences.en: And this was, I don't know, the third, the fourth time they've asked the court to hear the issue.
sentences.zh: 而且这是他们不知道第几次、第三次还是第四次要求法院审理此案。

sentences.en: And it was a surprise when they did, because it doesn't seem like the perfect vehicle to decide the question.
sentences.zh: 当他们这么做时，这令人感到意外，因为这似乎不是裁决该问题的绝佳载体。

sentences.en: This case has a lot of complications.
sentences.zh: 这个案子有很多复杂之处。

sentences.en: And yet the court, nevertheless, issued this major ruling, giving President Trump and other presidents a lot of power to do stuff unchecked by the lower courts.
sentences.zh: 然而，法院仍然发布了这一重大裁决，赋予了特朗普总统和其他总统巨大的权力，可以做一些不受下级法院制衡的事情。

sentences.en: And so basically, this ruling makes it so that all those other cases you just mentioned where judges issued universal injunctions that apply to the whole country,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这项裁决使得你刚才提到的所有其他案件——即法官发布适用于整个国家的普遍禁令的案件——

sentences.en: all of that could be moot.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都可能变得毫无意义。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court is basically taking a huge power away from the lower courts.
sentences.zh: 最高法院基本上剥夺了下级法院的一项巨大权力。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Adam, I want to understand the ruling a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我想更多地了解这项裁决。

sentences.en: And specifically, can you help us understand the majority's legal reasoning here?
sentences.zh: 具体来说，你能帮我们理解多数派这里的法律推理吗？

sentences.en: How did they explain why these nationwide injunctions were so problematic?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何解释为什么这些全国性禁令如此具有问题性的？

sentences.en: The majority opinion is written by Justice Amy Coney Barrett.
sentences.zh: 多数派意见由大法官埃米·科尼·巴雷特撰写。

sentences.en: It's the biggest decision of her career.
sentences.zh: 这是她职业生涯中最重要的决定。

sentences.en: It's quite a surprising assignment for such a junior justice to get.
sentences.zh: 对于如此年轻的大法官来说，分配到这样的任务相当令人惊讶。

sentences.en: She writes for the sixth justice conservative majority, all of the Republican appointees.
sentences.zh: 她代表由六名保守派多数派（全部由共和党任命）撰写意见。

sentences.en: All three of the Democratic appointees are in dissent.
sentences.zh: 三名民主党任命的大法官全部持反对意见。

sentences.en: And her argument is kind of a classic originalist take on the question.
sentences.zh: 她的论点可以说是关于该问题的一种经典的原始主义观点。

sentences.en: She says that when Congress passed the Judiciary Act of 1789, it gave courts some powers, but it didn't give them this power.
sentences.zh: 她说，当国会通过1789年《司法法》时，它赋予了法院一些权力，但并没有赋予他们这项权力。

sentences.en: And it looked back at English law, and basically, it was what conservatives often go to, which
sentences.zh: 它回顾了英国法律，基本上，这就是保守派经常回归的东西，即

sentences.en: is tradition and history, and less what's the better way to address an executive who is claiming huge powers.
sentences.zh: 传统和历史，而较少关注如何更好地应对一个声称拥有巨大权力的行政部门。

sentences.en: So let me read you a couple snippets from the decision.
sentences.zh: 所以让我读给你听裁决中的几个片段。

sentences.en: Justice Barrett writes, universal injunctions were not a feature of federal court litigation until sometime in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特大法官写道，直到20世纪的某个时候，普遍禁令都不是联邦法院诉讼的一个特点。

sentences.en: She goes on to say they remained rare until the turn of the 21st century, and that one study has identified approximately 127 universal injunctions between 1963 and 2023.
sentences.zh: 她接着说，直到21世纪初，它们仍然很少见，并且一项研究表明，在1963年至2023年期间，大约识别出了127项普遍禁令。

sentences.en: But 96 of those, over three quarters, were issued during the administrations of George W.
sentences.zh: 但在其中96项中，即超过四分之三，是在小布什、

sentences.en: Bush, Barack
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·

sentences.en: Obama, President Trump, and President Biden.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马、特朗普总统和拜登总统执政期间发布的。

sentences.en: So she makes the case that this is a recent concoction and therefore, under originalist thinking, quite suspect.
sentences.zh: 因此她提出，这是近代拼凑出来的产物，因此按照原始主义的思想，是非常可疑的。

sentences.en: So focusing on history, she says, the bottom line, question mark?
sentences.zh: 所以聚焦于历史，她说，最底线是什么，问号？

sentences.en: The universal injunction was conspicuously non-existent for most of our nation's history.
sentences.zh: 在我国历史的大部分时间里，普遍禁令明显是不存在的。

sentences.en: Had federal courts believed themselves to possess the tool, surely they would not have let it lay idle.
sentences.zh: 如果联邦法院认为自己拥有这种工具，他们肯定不会让它闲置不用。

sentences.en: So basically, Justice Barrett is saying, look, I've looked into the history of what our system from the start envisioned as the power of the federal courts.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，巴雷特大法官是在说，看，我研究了我们体制从一开始就设想的联邦法院权力的历史。

sentences.en: And it is not a system in which a single district judge can block the actions of the president for everybody in the country.
sentences.zh: 它并不是这样一个系统：单一的地区法官可以为全国所有人阻止总统的行动。

sentences.en: Like, that's just way too sweeping a power to give one particular judge.
sentences.zh: 比如说，赋予某一个特定法官的权力实在是太广泛了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So she's arguing that the two dozen or so universal injunctions issued since Trump took office for
sentences.zh: 所以她辩称，自从特朗普第二次上台以来发布的二十多项普遍禁令，

sentences.en: the second time are a vast overreach by federal judges who are claiming a power they do not possess.
sentences.zh: 是联邦法官严重的越权行为，他们声称拥有自己并不具备的权力。

sentences.en: Does she have a point here?
sentences.zh: 她有道理吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what you've just outlined does make some sense to me on paper.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你刚才概述的理论在纸面上确实对我有些道理。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lots of people think there are good reasons to be wary of universal injunctions.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为有充分的理由对普遍禁令保持警惕。

sentences.en: Another way to think about it is someone should decide whether these programs are lawful, but
sentences.zh: 另一种思考方式是，应该由某人来决定这些项目是否合法，但

sentences.en: maybe that should be the Supreme Court and not a judge who may have been cherry-picked by the litigants.
sentences.zh: 也许这应该是最高法院，而不是一个可能被诉讼当事人精挑细选出来的法官。

sentences.en: On the other side of the balance is we have a president here who is issuing a really aggressive
sentences.zh: 平衡的另一面是，我们这里有一位总统，他正在发布一套非常激进的

sentences.en: set of initiatives that will upend the way the nation works and that many people would say needs a prompt judicial reaction and needs to be paused while cases go forward.
sentences.zh: 倡议，这些倡议将颠覆国家运作的方式，许多人会说这需要迅速的司法反应，并且需要在案件推进的同时暂停执行。

sentences.en: Otherwise, the executive orders could be irreversible.
sentences.zh: 否则，行政命令可能是不可逆转的。

sentences.en: The idea here being, in other words, that this president, as we've mentioned, has been testing
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这里的想法是，正如我们所提到的，这位总统一直在

sentences.en: the boundaries of the law so frequently and in so many ways that you need the tool of universal injunctions.
sentences.zh: 如此频繁且以如此多的方式试探法律的边界，以至于你需要普遍禁令这个工具。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And remember, too, these are provisional rulings.
sentences.zh: 并且还要记住，这些是临时裁决。

sentences.en: These just freeze the status quo while the case goes ahead and the merits will be decided eventually.
sentences.zh: 这些只是在案件推进且最终将裁决实质问题时冻结现状。

sentences.en: And the question is, if Donald Trump wakes up one morning and issues an executive order, does that, like, presumptively stay in place for a couple of years while the case wins its
sentences.zh: 问题在于，如果唐纳德·特朗普某天早晨醒来发布了一项行政命令，这是否意味着该命令假定在案件通过法院审理的几年内一直保持原样？

sentences.en: way through the courts?
sentences.zh: 或者联邦法官能否早点看一眼并说，你知道吗，我认为这不合法，我要给予它应有的考虑。

sentences.en: Or can a federal judge have an early look and say, you know what, I don't think this is lawful and I'm going to give it due consideration.
sentences.zh: 但在此期间，我要冻结现状。

sentences.en: But in the meantime, I'm going to freeze the status quo.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我有疑问的地方，因为假设他确实发布了一项行政命令。

sentences.en: Well, that's what I have a question about, because let's say he does issue an executive order.
sentences.zh: 如果普遍禁令这个工具不可用，在弄清楚某事是否合法整个过程中，巴雷特

sentences.en: If this tool of universal injunctions is not available, what, if anything, does Barrett and
sentences.zh: 和其余多数派说有什么可以取代它，如果有的话？

sentences.en: the rest of the majority say could take its place during the whole process of figuring out whether something is legal?
sentences.zh: 巴雷特大法官确实说过有几种替代途径可以达到类似的效果。

sentences.en: Justice Barrett did say there were a few alternative routes to get to something like the same place.
sentences.zh: 她关注的主要途径是集体诉讼。

sentences.en: And the main one she focused on was class actions.
sentences.zh: 集体诉讼是一种案件，其中几名具名的原告代表一整类人。

sentences.en: A class action is a kind of case where a few named plaintiffs represent a whole class of people.
sentences.zh: 如果他们赢了，所有这些人都能获得法院裁决的好处。

sentences.en: And if they win, all of those people get the benefits of the court's ruling.
sentences.zh: 而这种方法，没有人会争辩它是合法的。

sentences.en: And that kind of approach, nobody disputes, is lawful.
sentences.zh: 现在，集体诉讼是繁琐的。

sentences.en: Now, class actions are cumbersome.
sentences.zh: 最高法院一直在试图缩减它们。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court has been trying to cut back on them.
sentences.zh: 但那是巴雷特大法官建议可以作为普遍禁令替代方案的主要载体。

sentences.en: But that is the primary vehicle that Justice Barrett suggests could be an alternative to universal injunctions.
sentences.zh: 那么这项裁决对终止出生公民权的行政命令到底意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: So what does this ruling mean altogether for the executive order to end birthright citizenship?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有一个有趣的转折。

sentences.en: Well, there's an interesting wrinkle.
sentences.zh: 法院表示其裁决将在30天内不生效。

sentences.en: The court says its ruling will not go into effect for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 这意味着挑战者将在至少几个不同的层面仓促应对。

sentences.en: And that means that challengers are going to scramble on at least a couple different levels.
sentences.zh: 就在裁决下达的同一天周五，我们已经提起了两起集体诉讼。

sentences.en: We've already had two class actions filed on Friday, the same day the decision came down.
sentences.zh: 有一个相当大的可能性，一个或多个法院再次在全国范围内叫停这件事。

sentences.en: There's a decent chance that one or more courts, again, shut the thing down across the nation.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有发生这种情况，我们将最终进入一个怪异、奇妙的世界。

sentences.en: But if that doesn't happen, we're going to end up in a weird, curious world.
sentences.zh: 22个州对出生公民权命令提出了挑战，并且他们赢了。

sentences.en: 22 states challenged the birthright citizenship order, and they won.
sentences.zh: 而这些胜利仍然保持有效。

sentences.en: And those victories remain in place.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果在30天结束时没有任何进展，我们将拥有一个拼凑的局面：在20多个州，

sentences.en: So if at the end of 30 days we don't have any movement, we'll have a patchwork with 20-plus
sentences.zh: 那里的系统规定在那里出生的儿童是公民，而在全国其他地方则不是。

sentences.en: states having a system where children born there are citizens and in the rest of the country not.
sentences.zh: 好的，但为了澄清，这种拼凑系统的整个问题在短期和长期内都可能是完全无关紧要的，对吧？

sentences.en: Okay, but just to be clear, this whole issue of the patchwork system could be totally moot in the short-term and in the long-term, right?
sentences.zh: 因为从理论上讲，某个案件可能会一直闹到最高法院，该案直接关于出生公民权以及它是否合宪。

sentences.en: Because theoretically, some case could wind its way up to the Supreme Court that is directly about birthright citizenship and whether it is constitutional.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，最高法院似乎很可能会裁决支持保留出生公民权，并反对总统的行政命令。

sentences.en: And as you've said, it seems likely that the Supreme Court would rule in favor of keeping birthright citizenship and against the president's executive order.
sentences.zh: 所以在那种情况下，这个出生公民权的整个问题就彻底平息了。

sentences.en: So in that instance, this whole birthright citizenship issue, that just gets put to reSt.
sentences.zh: 一切都恢复到你知道的160年来的老样子。

sentences.en: Everything reverts to the way it was, you know, for 160 years.
sentences.zh: 然而，推翻全国性禁令的问题将依然存在。

sentences.en: However, the issue of overturning nationwide injunctions would remain.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带回了对话开始时的观点：这个案件关乎比你是否因为在这里出生而成为公民要宏大得多的事情。

sentences.en: And that brings us back to the point at the beginning of the conversation that this case is about something much bigger than just whether you are a citizen if you were born here.
sentences.zh: 我理解得对吗？

sentences.en: Do I have that right?
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个案件的背景是一位正在推行最激进政策的总统。

sentences.en: I mean, this case arises against the backdrop of a president who is pushing the most aggressive
sentences.zh: 总统

sentences.en: program in living memory, perhaps in American history, testing the boundaries of the law.
sentences.zh: 这是活人记忆中、也许是美国历史上史无前例的项目，它正在对法律的边界进行测试。

sentences.en: And the three dissenting justices wrote scathing dissents in which they said the majority had taken
sentences.zh: 三位持异议的大法官撰写了严厉的反对意见，他们在其中表示，多数派在形式历史分析上犯下了

sentences.en: a profound wrong turn in formal historical analysis at the expense of the reality of withdrawing the main
sentences.zh: 严重的路线错误，而付出的代价却是剥夺了法官们用来遏制这个极具侵略性的行政机构的核心

sentences.en: tool that judges have used to keep this very aggressive administration in check.
sentences.zh: 工具这一现实。

sentences.en: I've heard a lot of dissents in my day.
sentences.zh: 我在这些年里听过很多反对意见。

sentences.en: And these dissents from the three Democratic appointees were really harsh and really thought that democracy was in peril.
sentences.zh: 这三位由民主党任命的大法官提出的反对意见确实非常严厉，他们真心认为民主制度正处于危险之中。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是韦娜·刘（Wena Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块字谜之一“连连看（Connections）”的创作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基（Sam Mazursky），我每天都制作拼字游戏（Spelling Bee）和 Letterboxd 游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由刚才你们听到的那些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: Adam, as you mentioned earlier, the ruling was 6-3, with the court's three liberal justices dissenting, pretty ferociously, actually.
sentences.zh: 亚当，正如你刚才提到的，裁决结果是6比3，法院的三位自由派大法官提出了反对意见，而且实际上相当激烈。

sentences.en: Can you explain their response and why it was as strong as it was?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下他们的反应以及为什么会有如此强烈的反应吗？

sentences.en: Well, the main dissent was written by Justice Sonia Sotomayor, joined by Justices Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown-Jackson.
sentences.zh: 嗯，主要的反对意见由大法官索尼娅·索托马约尔撰写，大法官埃ena·卡根和凯坦吉·布朗·杰克逊也加入了联署。

sentences.en: And Justice Sonia Sotomayor did something that justices very seldom do.
sentences.zh: 大法官索尼娅·索托马约尔做了一件大法官们极少做的事。

sentences.en: She read major portions of her dissent from the bench, which is a sign of profound disagreement.
sentences.zh: 她在审判席上宣读了她反对意见的主要部分，这是一个强烈反对的信号。

sentences.en: She thought the court had gone badly astray.
sentences.zh: 她认为法院已经严重误入歧途。

sentences.en: Let me just give you a taste of her opinion, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 雷切尔，让我来让你大致了解一下她的意见。

sentences.en: She says no right is safe in the new legal regime the court creates.
sentences.zh: 她说，在法院建立的新法律体制下，没有任何权利是安全的。

sentences.en: Today, the threat is to birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 今天，受到威胁的是出生公民权。

sentences.en: Tomorrow, a different administration may try to seize firearms from law-abiding citizens or prevent people of certain faiths from gathering to worship.
sentences.zh: 明天，另一个行政当局可能会试图没收守法公民的枪支，或者阻止特定信仰的人群聚集做礼拜。

sentences.en: The majority holds that, absent cumbersome class action litigation, courts cannot enjoin even such plainly unlawful policies.
sentences.zh: 多数派认为，如果没有繁琐的集体诉讼，法院甚至无法对这种明显非法的政策发出禁令。

sentences.en: So she sees a very broad threat to all kinds of freedoms, and not only freedoms that conservatives
sentences.zh: 因此，她看到了对各种自由的广泛威胁，不仅是保守派

sentences.en: like or liberals like, but to the very texture and nature of the American experience.
sentences.zh: 或自由派喜欢的自由，而是对美国经历的整个纹理和本质的威胁。

sentences.en: So Sotomayor clearly not satisfied with the alternatives, including class actions, that
sentences.zh: 所以索托马约尔显然对巴雷特和其他保守派大法官在这里建议的包括

sentences.en: Barrett and the conservative justices have suggested here.
sentences.zh: 集体诉讼在内的替代方案并不满意。

sentences.en: And she also sees this as setting up a terrible precedent that could be taken advantage of by future administrations.
sentences.zh: 她还认为这开创了一个糟糕的先例，可能会被未来的行政当局利用。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But Justice Sotomayor is meeting Justice Barrett on the legal arguments.
sentences.zh: 但索托马约尔大法官是在法律论点上与巴雷特大法官正面交锋。

sentences.en: A separate dissent, maybe an even hotter dissent, comes from Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson writing only for herself.
sentences.zh: 另一份独立的反对意见，或许是更激烈的反对意见，来自仅代表她自己的大法官凯坦吉·布朗·杰克逊。

sentences.en: And she says the majority's decision lets the executive branch violate the Constitution with respect to anyone who hasn't sued, anyone who's not a party.
sentences.zh: 她说，多数派的决定允许行政分支对任何未起诉的人、任何非诉讼当事人的人违反宪法。

sentences.en: And she says that's, quote, an existential threat to the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 她说这是，引述一下，“对法治的生存威胁”。

sentences.en: Justice Jackson makes the point that the majority creates kind of a two-tiered system.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊大法官指出，多数派制造了一种双轨系统。

sentences.en: There are people with money and lawyers and the wherewithal to go to court and get relief.
sentences.zh: 有些人有钱、有律师，还有去法院寻求救济的财力和能力。

sentences.en: But a lot of people don't have that.
sentences.zh: 但很多人没有这些。

sentences.en: And she says that's a real flaw in the court's reasoning as well.
sentences.zh: 她认为这也是法院推理中的一个真正缺陷。

sentences.en: So it sounds like Jackson is basically saying, we're in a new legal world here with this ruling.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来杰克逊基本上是在说，随着这项裁决，我们身处一个全新的法律世界中。

sentences.en: Lots of Americans will have their rights violated by the president.
sentences.zh: 许多美国人的权利将遭到总统的侵犯。

sentences.en: And the only way that they can fight it is if they sue the government, which most people just do not have the time or the resources to do.
sentences.zh: 而他们反击的唯一途径就是起诉政府，而大多数人根本没有时间或资源这样做。

sentences.en: And they're going to be forced to do that because these injunctions are no longer here to protect us against executive branch overreach.
sentences.zh: 他们将被迫这样做，因为这些禁令已不再能保护我们免受行政分支越权的侵害。

sentences.en: And so effectively, with this ruling, all of a sudden, all of us here in the United States
sentences.zh: 因此，实际上，随着这项裁决的出台，突然之间，我们美国的所有人

sentences.en: would have to become legal combatants, essentially, to protect basic rights enshrined in the
sentences.zh: 本质上都必须成为法律斗争的参与者，以保护宪法赋予的

sentences.en: Constitution.
sentences.zh: 基本权利。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, her language is just this side of apocalyptic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她的用词几乎带有世界末日般的色彩。

sentences.en: She says the majority's complicity in the creation of a culture of disdain for lower courts,
sentences.zh: 她说，多数派串通一气，助长了一种蔑视下级法院、

sentences.en: their rulings, and the law will surely hasten the downfall of our governing institutions, enabling our collective demise.
sentences.zh: 蔑视其裁决和法律的文化，这肯定会加速我们治理机构的垮台，导致我们的集体消亡。

sentences.en: So clearly, she's not mincing her words.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，她没有隐瞒自己的观点。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And Justice Barrett did not appreciate that commentary.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特大法官对这种评论并不赞赏。

sentences.en: And here we saw really a quite unusual thing, where the two most junior members of the court were really going at each other and in tones that were quite remarkable.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们看到了一个非常不同寻常的现象，法院中资历最浅的两名成员真的在针锋相对，而且语气相当引人注目。

sentences.en: Barrett, writing for the majority, says, we will not dwell on Justice Jackson's argument,
sentences.zh: 巴雷特在代表多数派发言时表示，我们不会纠缠于杰克逊大法官的论点，

sentences.en: which is at odds with more than two centuries' worth of precedent, not to mention the Constitution itself.
sentences.zh: 该论点与两个多世纪的判例背道而驰，更不用说宪法本身了。

sentences.en: We observe only this.
sentences.zh: 我们只想指出这一点。

sentences.en: Justice Jackson decries an imperial executive while embracing an imperial judiciary.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊大法官在谴责一个帝王般的行政分支的同时，却在拥抱一个帝王般的司法分支。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Can you just translate that for us, Adam?
sentences.zh: 亚当，你能为我们翻译一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Barrett is saying that the majority ruling is modeSt.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特是在说多数派的裁决是适度的。

sentences.en: It wants to stop judges from being activists.
sentences.zh: 它希望阻止法官成为激进分子。

sentences.en: It wants to keep everyone in their own lanes.
sentences.zh: 它希望让每个人都各司其职。

sentences.en: And according to her, Justice Jackson wants judges to decide everything, even things that ought to be decided by the elected branches.
sentences.zh: 据她所说，杰克逊大法官希望法官对一切事情做出裁决，甚至包括那些本应由民选机构决定的事情。

sentences.en: Like, she's basically saying, Justice Jackson doesn't want an imperious president, but she's perfectly happy with judges overreaching.
sentences.zh: 就像，她基本上是在说，杰克逊大法官不想要一个专横的总统，但她对法官越权却感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: That's her view.
sentences.zh: 这就是她的看法。

sentences.en: But they're operating on two different levels.
sentences.zh: 但他们是在两个不同的层面上运作。

sentences.en: One side is saying, and you can find this persuasive or not, but Justice Barrett is saying, you look at the legal materials, you look at history, you look at tradition, you look at
sentences.zh: 一方在说——你可能会觉得这有说服力，也可能不觉得——但巴雷特大法官是在说，你看看法律材料，你看看历史，你看看传统，你看看

sentences.en: the governing statute, and you come to a conclusion.
sentences.zh: 管辖法规，然后你得出结论。

sentences.en: And Justice Jackson is saying, the conclusion you have led us to is one in which the president of the United States can largely do whatever he wants.
sentences.zh: 而杰克逊大法官则在说，你们引导我们得出的结论是，美国总统基本上可以为所欲为。

sentences.en: Basically, you guys are minding the details, but you're ignoring the practical realities of your decision.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你们在关注细节，但你们却忽视了你们决定的实际现实。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: But Justice Barrett feels that the upshot of Justice Jackson's dissent is actually to give too much power to the federal courts.
sentences.zh: 但巴雷特觉得，杰克逊反对意见的结果实际上是赋予了联邦法院太多的权力。

sentences.en: And Barrett quotes Justice Jackson's own words against her.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特以其人之道还治其人之身，引用了杰克逊大法官自己的话。

sentences.en: Barrett says, Justice Jackson would do well to heed her own admonition.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特说，杰克逊大法官最好听从她自己的忠告。

sentences.en: And then quoting from Jackson, everyone from the president on down is bound by law.
sentences.zh: 然后引用杰克逊的话说，从总统向下的每个人都受法律约束。

sentences.en: The suggestion being that the dissenters also need to follow the law.
sentences.zh: 暗示的意思是异议者也需要遵守法律。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It really sounds like Barrett is basically throwing Jackson's words back in her face.
sentences.zh: 这听起来确实像是巴雷特把杰克逊的话狠狠地甩回给了她。

sentences.en: Is it usually this pointed and personal?
sentences.zh: 平时通常会这么尖锐和针对个人吗？

sentences.en: Well, back in the day before Justice Antonin Scalia died in 2016, he could write a biting sentence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在安东宁·斯卡利亚大法官于2016年去世之前，他就能写出犀利的句子。

sentences.en: But even then, there was an element of playfulness and humor to it.
sentences.zh: 但即使在那个时候，其中也带有某种嬉戏和幽默的成分。

sentences.en: This seemed quite raw.
sentences.zh: 这看起来相当原始和尖锐。

sentences.en: It kind of feels like in this back and forth between Jackson and Barrett, that this is actually
sentences.zh: 感觉在杰克逊和巴雷特之间的这种来回交锋中，这实际上

sentences.en: fundamentally about the power of the president versus the power of the courts and the balance between the two of them.
sentences.zh: 根本上是关于总统权力与法院权力之间的较量，以及两者之间的平衡。

sentences.en: That's right, Rachel, although I would draw a distinction.
sentences.zh: 没错，雷切尔，尽管我会做一个区分。

sentences.en: It is true that the majority amplifies executive power, presidential power, the power of President
sentences.zh: 诚然，多数派扩大了行政权力、总统权力、特朗普

sentences.en: Trump.
sentences.zh: 总统的权力。

sentences.en: And it's true that the dissent wants federal trial judges to be able to judge the lawfulness of Trump prograMs.
sentences.zh: 诚然，异议方希望联邦初审法官能够裁决特朗普计划的合法性。

sentences.en: But the place I might draw a slightly different distinction is I don't think the Supreme Court is eager to give up any of its own power.
sentences.zh: 但我可能要做出一点细微区分的地方是，我不认为最高法院渴望放弃它自己的任何权力。

sentences.en: While it doesn't think that lower court judges get to have the last word vis-a-vis the president, it at least wants to reserve for itself the right to do that.
sentences.zh: 虽然它认为下级法院法官在面对总统时没有最终发言权，但它至少希望为自己保留这样做的权利。

sentences.en: But at the same time, this is a court for the second term in a row on the last day of the term by a 6-3 vote manages to profoundly amplify presidential power.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，这是最高法院连续第二年在任期最后一天以6比3的投票结果，深刻地扩大了总统的权力。

sentences.en: Last year, it ruled in favor of then-presidential candidate Trump on the question of whether he was largely immune from prosecution.
sentences.zh: 去年，它在是否享有广泛免于起诉豁免权的问题上，做出了有利于时任总统候选人特朗普的裁决。

sentences.en: And in the process, sketched out a vision of a bold and energetic president unchecked by law in many realMs.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，它勾勒出了一种大胆而有朝气的总统愿景，在许多领域不受法律的约束。

sentences.en: And this year, it kind of vindicates and even further amplifies that vision of the presidency by saying that judges around the country can't tell the president what to do.
sentences.zh: 而今年，它通过表示全国各地的法官不能对总统指手画脚，进一步证实甚至扩展了这种总统职位的愿景。

sentences.en: And in both of the cases, the majority says, we are talking about the nature of executive power.
sentences.zh: 在这两个案件中，多数派都表示，我们谈论的是行政权力的性质。

sentences.en: It applies to all presidents.
sentences.zh: 它适用于所有总统。

sentences.en: It's not about any particular president.
sentences.zh: 这与任何特定总统无关。

sentences.en: But at least in the short term, it has profoundly helped President Trump.
sentences.zh: 但至少在短期内，它对特朗普总统有深远的帮助。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: It seems not unreasonable to say that it's difficult to divorce the two.
sentences.zh: 说这两者很难撇清关系，似乎并非不合理。

sentences.en: Given this new understanding of presidential versus judicial power, if you are President
sentences.zh: 鉴于对总统权力与司法权力这种新的理解，如果你是特朗普总统，

sentences.en: Trump, what becomes possible now that this ruling has been issued that perhaps was not possible before?
sentences.zh: 在这项裁决发布后，现在有哪些以前可能无法实现的事情变得可行了？

sentences.en: Well, for starters, he faces a couple dozen universal injunctions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，他面临着几十起普遍禁令。

sentences.en: And I think he might well be able to go to court and get some or all of them dissolved.
sentences.zh: 我认为他很可能会去法院解除其中部分或全部禁令。

sentences.en: On issues, just to be clear, like firing federal workers, defunding federal agencies that you talked about earlier.
sentences.zh: 明确一下，在诸如解雇联邦员工、停止为你刚才提到的联邦机构提供资金等问题上。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Adam, do you think that there's any chance that the government's goal all along with this birthright citizenship executive order and the obvious challenges that were going
sentences.zh: 亚当，你认为政府从一开始就带着这种出生公民权行政令以及势必会带来的挑战，有没有这种可能，

sentences.en: to come to it, do you think that they intended from the beginning that this was going to be
sentences.zh: 你认为他们从一开始就打算让这

sentences.en: something that would ultimately help them not end birthright citizenship, but expand executive power the way that you have just explained?
sentences.zh: 最终成为一件能够帮助他们实现以下目标的事情——不是终止出生公民权，而是像你刚才解释的那样扩大行政权力？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Well, whether this was strategic brilliance or happenstance, what transpired was that the
sentences.zh: 嗯，不管这是战略上的精妙绝伦还是机缘巧合，最终发生的事情是，

sentences.en: administration gained one of its most dearly sought goals, which is not to let judges block its initiatives and programs and judge the lawfulness of the Trump agenda.
sentences.zh: 行政当局实现了它最渴望的目标之一，那就是不让法官阻止其倡议和计划，也不让法官裁决特朗普议程的合法性。

sentences.en: Now, the immediate consequence of the court's ruling might be a lot more litigation because
sentences.zh: 现在，法院裁决的直接后果可能是更多的诉讼，因为

sentences.en: it may be that a lot of individuals are going to feel they need to have to sue because they don't have the benefit of universal injunctions.
sentences.zh: 很多个人可能会觉得他们必须起诉，因为他们无法享受普遍禁令的好处。

sentences.en: But the big picture is we have a president who's quite happy with the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 但大局是，我们有一位对最高法院相当满意的总统。

sentences.en: So we see a kind of close relationship, a dynamic relationship between the president and the
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到了总统与最高法院之间一种紧密的、动态的关系，总统为自己宣称前所未有的权力，

sentences.en: Supreme Court with the president claiming unprecedented powers for himself and the court not only not standing in his way, but generally opening the door.
sentences.zh: 而法院不仅没有挡路，反而普遍为之敞开了大门。

sentences.en: Adam, thank you for spending part of your weekend with us.
sentences.zh: 亚当，谢谢你和我们度过周末的一部分时间。

sentences.en: It's good to be here, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，雷切尔。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Sunday, the Senate started debate on President Trump's domestic policy package.
sentences.zh: 周日，参议院开始就特朗普总统的国内政策一揽子计划展开辩论。

sentences.en: It's not clear if GOP leaders have enough support to pass the measure by their deadline of July 4th.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚共和党领导人是否有足够的支持在7月4日的最后期限前通过该法案。

sentences.en: Although many Republicans hailed the tax cuts and reductions to Medicaid and other social programs,
sentences.zh: 尽管许多共和党人对减税以及削减医疗补助和其他社会计划表示欢迎，

sentences.en: Democrats universally assailed the bill, which a new analysis says would add at least $3.3 trillion to the federal deficit over the next 10 years.
sentences.zh: 但民主党人一致猛烈抨击该法案，一项新的分析称，该法案将在未来10年内给联邦赤字增加至少3.3万亿美元。

sentences.en: And Republican Senator Tom Tillis of North Carolina says he will not seek re-election next year, in part because of his opposition to the bill.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州共和党参议员汤姆·蒂利斯表示，他明年将不再寻求连任，部分原因是他反对该法案。

sentences.en: His announcement came a day after President Trump threatened to back a primary challenger against him because Tillis would not fall in line.
sentences.zh: 此前一天，特朗普总统威胁要支持该州的初选挑战者来对抗他，因为蒂利斯不肯服从。

sentences.en: His departure is sure to set off a competitive race in North Carolina that could be pivotal in the battle for control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他的离去肯定会在北卡罗来纳州引发一场竞争激烈的竞选，这可能对争夺参议院控制权的战斗至关重要。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Diana Wynn, Rochelle Bonja, and Rob Zipko.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由戴安娜·温（Diana Wynn）、罗谢尔·邦贾（Rochelle Bonja）和罗布·齐普科（Rob Zipko）制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willans and Rachel Quester.
sentences.zh: 由帕特里夏·威兰斯（Patricia Willans）和雷切尔·克斯特（Rachel Quester）剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Alicia Baetup and Marian Lozano.
sentences.zh: 包含艾莉西亚·拜托普（Alicia Baetup）和玛丽安·洛扎诺（Marian Lozano）的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 由阿莉莎·莫克斯利（Alyssa Moxley）进行混音工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Bunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由来自 Wonderly 的吉姆·邦伯格（Jim Bunberg）和本·兰兹伯格（Ben Landsberg）创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢迈克尔·巴尔巴罗（Michael Barbaro）。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》（The Daily）。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯（Rachel Abrams）。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时甚至令人惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都市》（Metro）的最新一期节目中，我和萨拉·科尼格（Sarah Koenig）将为您讲述人们试图保持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 都市。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
